title: 3D-Flow: Flow-based Standard Cell Legalization for 3D ICs
problem: Standard-cell placement legalization in 3D ICs must resolve overflows across multiple dies while minimizing cell displacement; traditional 2D legalizers are inefficient for 3D geometry.
motivation: 3D IC integration enables higher density but complicates physical design; legalizers must minimize displacement while respecting multi-die constraints.
method: Proposes 3D-Flow, a flow-based legalization algorithm that models the 3D space as a grid graph and finds shortest augmenting paths to resolve overflowed bins; uses branch-and-bound for path optimization and cycle-canceling post-optimization to minimize maximum displacement.
key_novelty: Network flow formulation for 3D cell legalization leveraging global multi-die perspective to minimize displacement.
contributions: 3D grid graph representation of multi-die layout for flow-based legalization
Branch-and-bound algorithm for shortest augmenting path computation
Cycle-canceling post-optimization for maximum displacement minimization
Up to 13% and 43% less average and maximum cell displacement vs SOTA with similar runtime

metrics.other: 13% reduction in average cell displacement; 43% in maximum displacement

limitations: Not discussed—focuses on algorithmic efficiency without analyzing scalability to extremely large designs.
primary_theme: Network flow-based legalization for 3D IC placement
